names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 29 aprilie, «Sfântul Ierarh Vasile de Ostrog».
His name at baptism, as doxologia.ro's life prints it: «La botez a primit numele Stoian».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 29 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Βασίλειος ο Θαυματουργός εκ Σερβίας», with the rank word, the epithet and the country left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 29. април ст. ст., „Св. Василије Острошки.“, with Св. left off as no rank. Острошки — of Ostrog, where he ended his life and where his relics are — is an epithet and not a rank `honorific.js` composes, so it is kept, and the fuller form is what keeps this folder **out** of the bare «Василије» fold the corpus's five other Basils share. The see of Zahumlje and Skenderija and the rank of metropolitan are the body's and belong to `office` and `types`.

The nominative of the day's own line, «Свт. Василия Острожского», and the form life6921 titles him with, «Святитель Василий, чудотворец Острожский», with the rank words taken off. THE NAME PAGE PUTS THE OTHER SEE WHERE A SURNAME WOULD GO: 381 heads «Святой Василий, епископ Захолмский», where «Захолмский» is inside the office rather than beside the name, and life6491 heads him «Святитель Василий Захолмский, Скендерийский (Острожский, Требинский, Сербский)» — five toponymics at once, of which the stored form keeps the one the day line itself uses and the one the folder's Serbian form «Василије Острошки» already carries. The bare «Василий» is one of this corpus's widest folds, which is why a toponymic is kept: measured against the gate's own key function, 'василии острожскии' has no other holder.

birth.note: doxologia.ro's life: «S-a născut la 28 decembrie 1610 în satul Mrkonjić din Herțegovina».

death.note: doxologia.ro's life: «Sfântul Vasile a trecut la Domnul la 29 aprilie 1671, în chilia sa de la Ostrog».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 29 апреля ст. ст. — «Свт. Василия Острожского (1671) (Серб.).»

attestations.note: The day's fifth entry of eight, marked «(Серб.)», which is how this calendar flags a commemoration it keeps from the Serbian church. Index 381 serves THREE readings of him — life6921, life6491 and life954 — and all three head «Дни памяти: 29 апреля , 30 августа (Серб.)»; the 29 апреля day page is the one that lists him and is the day recorded here, and THE «30 августа (Серб.)» DAY PAGE WAS NOT READ. THE THREE READINGS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER ABOUT HIS CENTURY AND HIS `dates` DID NOT MOVE: life6921 opens «Святитель Василий родился в 1610 году», which is the year the folder already holds off doxologia; life954 says he was born «в XVI веке в Поповой волости в Герцеговине» and held the see «во 2-й половине XVI века», a hundred years earlier, as the successor of a bishop Pavle and the predecessor of a bishop Nikodim. The day's own line heads him «(1671)», which is the death year the folder already holds. Widening a birth of 1610 to cover a whole earlier century would invent an interval no source gives, and the folder's two flat years are each read from a page that states them, so nothing moved and the disagreement is recorded. Both hymns the day page prints under his name are added here.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 29 aprilie — «Sfântul Ierarh Vasile de Ostrog»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 29ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Βασίλειος ο Θαυματουργός εκ Σερβίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 29 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and it is plainly the same man: born 1610 of devout parents, a monk of the Dormition monastery of Trebinje, bishop of Zahumlje, a wonderworker, dead in peace in 1671 and buried at Ostrog in Montenegro near the Herzegovinian border. **The Greek adds three things**: the district of his birth, «στην περιοχή του Πόποβ της Ερζεγοβίνης», Popovo in Herzegovina; that he left his father's house out of love for the monastic life; that his see was «Ζάκχολμσκ και Σκεντερίας», Zahumlje and Skenderija, and that he came to it as successor of the bishop Paul and predecessor of the bishop Nikodemos; and that he visited the Holy Mountain in order to learn the Byzantine monastic and hesychast tradition. **The page also contradicts itself about when he took the throne** — «Ανέλαβε τον Μητροπολιτικό θρόνο στο δεύτερο ήμισυ του 16ου αιώνα», the second half of the sixteenth century, which cannot stand with the 1610 birth it prints in the same paragraph and in its own head «(1610 - 1671)». The contradiction is recorded and not corrected, and **this folder's existing `dates`, 1610 and 1671 off doxologia, were left untouched**, because the Greek gives the same two years and nothing narrower. It prints no hymn and names no relic beyond the burial at Ostrog.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 12.05.2026 (29. април ст. ст.) — „Св. Василије Острошки.“

attestations.note: The fullest account of this man read for this folder, and by a Serbian bishop writing of a Serbian saint. **No date was taken, and the refusal is arithmetic.** The entry closes „Престави се мирно Господу, у XVI веку“ — he reposed in the **sixteenth** century — where doxologia's life gives his birth as 28 December 1610 and his death as 29 April 1671, which are the two years this folder records. Widening the death to hold a sixteenth-century repose would make the folder say he died before he was born, and narrowing or displacing a sourced year is not a reader's act either, so **nothing was touched**. What this does change is the weight of a disagreement already written into this life: saint.gr puts him on the metropolitan throne in the second half of the sixteenth century while giving the same 1610 for his birth, and the Prologue is now **a second source for that century against the two years**. The choice is the author's. **It also disagrees about the birthplace**: „Родом из Попова Села у Херцеговини“, where doxologia's life names the village Mrkonjić in Herzegovina — recorded and not resolved, and no `locations` were taken for either. New besides: parents simple but devout; the monastic habit taken at the **Trebinje monastery of the Dormition**; labour laid upon labour, each heavier than the last; the see of **Zahumlje and Skenderija** taken against his own will; the first residence at **Tvrdoš** and the flight to Ostrog when the Turks destroyed it; the flock guarded „од свирепства турског и лукавства латинског“; the relics whole and healing to this day; **Christians and Muslims alike** coming to them; and the great assembly of the people at Ostrog every year at Trinity, which is a moveable observance this schema has no field for and is therefore in the life and not in this row. The Prologue prints no hymn.

hymns.text: От юности твоея всего себе Господеви отдал еси,/ пребывая в молитвах, трудех и постех, отче Богоносне,/ образ был еси добродетели твоему стаду;/ сего ради видя Бог твое благое произволение,/ поставляет тя Своей Церкви пастыря и добраго архиерея/ и по преставлении твоем соблюде святое тело твое нерушимо, святителю Василие./ Темже, яко имея дерзновение,/ молися Христу Богу/ спастися душам нашим.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Тропарь святителя Василия, епископа Захолмского или Острожского (в Черногории, Cербского)», глас 4, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 29 апреля ст. ст.

english.text: From thy youth thou gavest thyself wholly to the Lord, abiding in prayers, in labours and in fasting, O God-bearing father, and thou wast a pattern of virtue to thy flock. Wherefore God, seeing thy good will, set thee over His Church as a shepherd and a good high priest, and after thy departure kept thy holy body incorrupt, O hierarch Basil. Therefore, having boldness, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Яко от младенства себе поработив Господеви,/ постом и бдением свое тело удручая, мудре,/ сосуд честен Духу Пресвятому явился еси,/ сего ради поставляет тя пастырем Своей Церкви,/ юже добре пасл еси./ Темже ко Господу отходиши, Егоже возлюбил еси./ Молимся ти, помяни и нас, верою чтущих святую память твою, да вси зовем ти:/ радуйся, всечестне отче Василие.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Кондак святителя Василия, епископа Захолмского или Острожского (в Черногории, Cербского)», глас 8, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 29 апреля ст. ст.

english.text: Having enslaved thyself to the Lord from infancy, and wisely wearing thy body down with fasting and vigil, thou wast shown to be a vessel of honour for the All-Holy Spirit; wherefore He sets thee as a shepherd over His Church, which thou didst shepherd well. Then thou departest to the Lord whom thou didst love. We pray thee, remember us also who honour thy holy memory with faith, that we all may cry to thee: rejoice, all-honoured father Basil.
